messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: continuous-batching-service (cb-serving-prod) reporting sustained latency cliff and elevated 5xxs across multiple zones. Pager: @eng-oncall. Metrics: latency p95 x4, error-rate 5%, KV cache evictions spiking.
anya: grabbing it — seeing KV eviction rate ~8000/min (baseline ~1k). microbatch_size distribution skewed: many requests hitting 64-128 instead of 8-16.
mike: Any recent rollouts?
anya: rolled prefetch heuristics v2 3h ago to reduce cold starts. Telemetry shows aggressive prefetch + continuous batching causing KV churning and larger batch coalescing under high concurrency.
ben: Oof. That explains the cache blowout. Users hitting hotspot prefixes, prefetch stuffing the cache and causing evictions -> more backend reads -> higher latency.
sarah: Customer impact: a handful of high-throughput customers reporting timeouts and elevated 429/504. Support ticket queue showing repeated complaints.
anya: Initial mitigation suggestion: disable prefetch-v2 for cb-serving-prod, force microbatch cap to 16, and enable jitter on batch window. Can do a config hotfix via orchestration.
zack: +1. Also we should throttle ingress for tiered customers briefly (token-bucket reduce) to avoid tail amplification.
mike: I can push the config change. Plan: 1) rollback prefetch-v2 -> prefetch-v1 2) set max_microbatch_size=16 3) set batch_window_jitter_ms=15-45. Apply to region eu-west-1 first.
anya: Sounds good. Deploy-bot, can you stage a canary?
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Starting rollout: cb-config-hotfix@canary -> region eu-west-1 (10% hosts). Triggered by mike. CI checks OK.
anya: While canary runs, we should snapshot KV metrics and trace one hot customer. Also prepare an emergency script to flush prefetch queue/backpressure if things worsen.
mike: Canary results at +3m: p95 down 30% on canary hosts, eviction-rate down 60% there. No spike in errors.
ben: Good sign. Ready to promote? Recommend progressive rollout 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 5m observation windows.
sarah: I'll notify support and SRE on duty to escalate if any major customers see regression. Draft note: "We've applied a temporary config hotfix to reduce batch amplification and rolled back prefetch heuristics for affected clusters. Monitoring closely; load should stabilize."
zack: Also add a short-term routing policy: route high-concurrency keys to lower-prefetch pool to avoid cross-tenant eviction storms. Ops runbook updated under /runbooks/cb-prefetch.
mike: Rolling to 50% now. deploy-bot: rollout to 50% complete.
anya: Observed system-wide: p95 trending down, error-rate sliding towards baseline. Still seeing a handful of long tails; investigating traces show KV lookups per request dropping from ~40 to ~12 after hotfix.
sarah: Customer-facing update posted to support threads; no SLA credit yet, but we are tracking affected customers.
ben: Postmortem action items so far: 1) revert prefetch-v2 until additional throttles/jitter in heuristics, 2) add guardrail to prevent prefetch from filling >20% of KV capacity, 3) telemetry alert for microbatch skew > 4x baseline, 4) automated rollback if eviction spike > 3x in 5m window.
zack: I'll own guardrail implementation.
mike: Morning on-call handoff: @anya will follow up with deeper root cause analysis and model-level traces. @zack will implement guardrail. @sarah will coordinate customer outreach.
anya: logging a ticket: INFR-4291 "prefetch-v2 induces KV blowup under high concurrency -> cb microbatch cliff". Putting current hotfix config as patch in the ticket.
sarah: Marking this thread for incident review. Closing active pager — moving to postmortem. If anything regresses, reopen channel. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: continuous-batching-service performance stabilized after config hotfix and staged rollback. Total mitigation time ~27m.
